title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper uses transaction-level data from 2021 to mid-February 2025 to analyze the structure and resilience of the euro-denominated repo market under financial stress. The research finds that the euro repo market exhibits a core-periphery network structure, with a small core of highly active institutions conducting most trading. Contrary to expectations, financial stress is associated with lower repo spreads, suggesting the market functions as a shock absorber rather than a amplifier of stress.
key_points: The euro repo market displays a core-periphery structure with a small core of highly active institutions conducting most trading
Connectivity between institutions, especially banks trading with other banks, has grown over time even during stress periods
At the sectoral level, trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable under stress
Financial stress is associated with lower spreads at the market level, consistent with the repo market functioning as a shock absorber
The euro repo market accounts for 56% of daily euro money market transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts
Total outstanding repo value increased 4.9% from June 2023 to June 2024
why_it_matters: Understanding repo market network dynamics is critical for financial stability oversight. The paper demonstrates that the euro repo market remains resilient during stress periods, with stable volumes and declining spreads. However, vulnerabilities can propagate through the system given NBFI involvement. This research informs policymakers on repo market regulation and financial stability frameworks that monitor both individual institutions and sector-level interconnections.
market_structure_context: The paper examines the network topology of euro repo market participants using transaction-level data from the SFTDS. Financial stress is measured using the Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress (CISS). Key network metrics (density, strength) are analyzed alongside repo variables (volumes, spreads, haircuts, maturities). The core-periphery structure intensifies connectivity during stress periods.
important_numbers: 56% of daily euro money market transactions
30% of outstanding amounts in euro money market
4.9% increase in outstanding repos from June 2023 to June 2024
notes: Source is an ECB Working Paper (No 3205) by Vanessa Schöller. Disclaimer notes views are the author's and not necessarily the ECB's. The paper analyzes euro-denominated repo transactions using network metrics and regression techniques. Key historical stress events discussed include 2007/2008 crisis, March 2020 US Treasury market stress (hedge fund basis trades), and September 2022 UK LDI fund gilt crisis.
